subject: Energy
title: Uranium: The Nuclear Fuel
description: Learn Uranium: The Nuclear Fuel in one minute.

hook.text: Uranium is the primary fuel for nuclear reactors—a heavy metal found in rocks and seawater worldwide.

buildup.text: Natural uranium is 99.3% U-238 and only 0.7% U-235—but U-235 is the fissile isotope that reactors need.

discovery.text: Enrichment increases the U-235 concentration to 3–5% for reactors—using centrifuges spinning at supersonic speeds.

twist.text: Weapons-grade uranium requires 90%+ enrichment—the same technology, pushed further, creates bomb material.

climax.text: That dual-use nature makes enrichment the most politically sensitive step in the nuclear fuel cycle.

punchline.text: Same element, same centrifuge—power plant or bomb.

quiz.question: What percentage of natural uranium is fissile U-235?
